_meta.description: Rolling registry of recent post generation characteristics. Used to inject differentiation context into future generation prompts, preventing hook repetition, title cadence cloning, and emotional arc duplication. Capped at 30 recent entries per category.
_meta.usage: Read by scripts/lib/generation-memory.js before generation. Written after each successful post creation. Pass result to generate-post.js as differentiation context.

recentHooks.hook: Contentment hums. Settling buzzes.
What if the thing you have been calling burnout for the last two years is not actually burnout?

Twelve tabs open. Two of them you forgot you opened. A podcast playing that you stopped hearing four minutes ago. Your phone buzzing in your pocket while you reach for it anyway, and underneath all of
Picture two people who both wake up at 5am to train.
Ask yourself something and notice what happens next. Not a big question. Something small, like what you actually want for dinner, or whether you want to go to that thing on Saturday.

It's a Tuesday afternoon and you just closed the fourth tab about "finding your calling" without reading it. You already know what it says. Journal your values. Sit with the discomfort. Trust the proc
Both of them make your stomach drop. That is the whole problem.
You closed your eyes to meditate and the anxiety got louder.

There is a specific kind of tired that has nothing to do with how hard you worked. You wake up foggy, a little ashamed, and you cannot point to a single thing you did that would justify feeling this w

A decision is sitting on your chest right now. You know exactly which one. You have known for weeks, maybe months. And every time it comes close to the surface, you find something urgent to do instead

The noise you are hearing right now is not coming from your mind. It is coming from the seventeen tabs you opened, the three group chats waiting on you, the podcast you half-heard at breakfast, and th
Here is a question that will sting a little. If someone offered you a million dollars to name your next direction in the next sixty seconds, could you do it?
Here's a question almost nobody asks before they start medicating a problem: what if the flatness you feel isn't a chemical shortage, but an accurate reading?

Here is the trap nobody warns you about. You are so overwhelmed you finally give yourself permission to stop. You collapse on the couch, open your phone, and three hours later you feel worse than befo
Here is something strange nobody explains: the more you consume that feels good in the moment, the emptier your tank gets by morning.
The word "discipline" got hijacked. Somewhere along the way it stopped meaning "I keep my word to myself" and started meaning "grind until you break, then post about it."

Here is a small experiment. Right now, count how many decisions you have half-researched this week and still not made. The apartment you keep comparing. The email you have drafted four times. The thin

Everybody told you to follow your passion. So you did. You followed it into a music project, then a podcast, then a candle business, then back to music. Each one felt electric for about three weeks. T

Most advice about changing your life assumes you want a bonfire. Quit the job. Sell the house. Fly to Bali and find yourself in a hostel. But you don't want a bonfire. You want the low hum of wrongnes

You sat down to work an hour ago. You have opened the same document four times, checked your phone twice, refilled your water, and read the same sentence enough times that the words stopped meaning an
Let me guess. You had plans for today. Real ones. The kind you wrote down because they mattered.
You already tried the mirror thing. You stood there, made eye contact with yourself, said "I am worthy, I am enough," and felt like a fraud with toothpaste on your chin.

You laughed at a joke last week and it felt like watching someone else laugh. Like you were standing slightly behind your own eyes, going through the motions, waiting to feel the thing you used to fee

Try this right now. Close your eyes and picture your "purpose." What shows up? Probably a foggy montage of you doing something meaningful, lit warmly, applauded quietly. Now open your eyes. Nothing ch
Have you ever said your own job title out loud and felt your throat tighten a little, like you were reciting someone else's line?
Picture the moment the grocery store lights start to hum too loud, the cart wheels squeak, someone's phone rings, and your chest tightens for no reason you can name. You are not in danger. Nothing is
Your body is done. Your eyes burn. You have work in six hours and every cell knows it. And still, your thumb keeps flicking upward, feeding the screen one more clip, one more post, one more nothing.

Comfort feels like a friend in the moment and a thief by nightfall. You take the easier road at 2pm, you feel relief for about twenty minutes, and then some quiet part of you starts collecting interes

Here is a strange test. Try to sit in a chair with nothing in your hands for two minutes. No phone, no music, no plan. Most people cannot do it. Their hand reaches for the phone before their brain eve
Here is a strange thing about tires spinning in mud. The engine is roaring. The wheels are moving fast. You are pouring in effort. And you are going absolutely nowhere.
